historical_delay_context.source: Friedrich Freiherr Kress von Kressenstein, Meine Mission im Kaukasus, memoir dated October 12, 1943; German-language edition published in Tbilisi, 2001.
locators: Memoir paragraph ending before printed page 50: delayed telegrams and radio range
Printed pages 62-63: first direct revolution news on the night of November 9/10
historical_delay_context.summary: Kress recalls that Berlin telegrams sometimes took weeks, that the initial equipment reached Constantinople but not Germany, and that the larger Tiflis station first received the German revolution announcement.
historical_delay_context.inference_limit: This supports the general possibility of delayed relay traffic, not the actual date, key or plaintext of p73. The memoir was written decades later.

p155_historical_context_reference.summary: Hopman records Asgard and Tresivolos arriving at Sevastopol at 09:00 on November 7, a decision to unload and return them to Poti, and Asgard leaving for Poti on November 9. This closely corroborates the p155 two-part shipping message.

calendar_hypothesis.observation: October 26 Julian corresponds to November 8 Gregorian in 1918, exactly matching the two printed dates.
calendar_hypothesis.status: unverified metadata hypothesis; not a date correction
calendar_hypothesis.counter_evidence: The Georgian National Archives exhibits a Transcaucasian Sejm law adopted on April 13, 1918 replacing the Julian calendar with the Gregorian calendar. Late-1918 German military radio traffic cannot simply be assumed to use Old Style dates.
calendar_hypothesis.prior_art_check: No explicit Julian/Gregorian discussion was found in the archived 2017 challenge comments. The underlying date discrepancy was already raised by Norbert and acknowledged by Lasry.
calendar_hypothesis.effect_on_analysis: Preserve both source date layers and both key-period possibilities. No ciphertext, key assignment or plaintext is changed.
